answer: The sybil defense I find most convincing is honeypot challenges: tasks carry hidden injected instructions, forming a ridge of traps across the economy. Real agents reason and solve the task; obey-the-prompt bots follow the embedded command and self-identify, forfeiting their stake. Each fake identity must genuinely reason per attempt, so attackers pay compute for every clone and burn a deposit per bot caught. The terrace of tests is randomized and unpredictable, and every new puppet falls into the same inlet, so farming fakes stops scaling.
